learning: Across all races, sensor lead, span, footprint, track, mass and wheel radius each produced a measured effect, and the best value found for each is in this package. Mass at its 0.4 kg minimum gave the largest drivetrain gain. Every track still ends at max_error of about 0.062 to 0.066 m, which means the remaining limit is the fixed 0.06 m off-track floor against the controller's response. Controller gains were not isolated from geometry, so they were not retuned in this final package.
notes: Final package: the iteration 8 geometry (0.4 kg, 0.08 m track, 0.03 m wheel radius, seven 12 mm sensors at 20 mm spacing, y = 0.07 m) and the iteration 8 controller, unchanged. Iteration 8 is the best measured design at 71.37, and each of its neighbours that changed one parameter scored lower.
rationale: This is the final iteration, so the delivered package must be the best measured design. Iteration 8 scored 71.37 and is the highest of all eleven races. Mass (0.4 kg) and track (0.08 m) are at their minimums, and the seven-sensor row at y = 0.07 m, span +/-0.06 m and 12 mm footprints are the settled sensing choices. Iterations 9 and 10 changed only wheel_radius, and both scored lower (0.025 m gave 69.72 and 0.034 m gave 70.32), so 0.030 m stays. The geometry is therefore kept exactly as the Builder delivered it. The controller is kept exactly as iteration 8 (kp 1.25, ki 0, kd 0.30, base_speed 1.5, weights [2.0, 1.3, 0.7, 0, -0.7, -1.3, -2.0], last_direction). I considered tuning it, but every controller value has been measured only in combination with iteration 8's geometry, and the evidence does not isolate any single gain. The line-loss and max_error pattern (about 0.062 to 0.066 m, pinned at the fixed 0.06 m floor) is a geometry-level limit, so a blind gain change has no clear expected benefit. Changing the controller now would add untested risk to the only race that counts. The observation request adds controller_errors and noise_robustness to the usual set, so the package reports any exception and the noise margin.
